_comment: DISCRIMINATION CONTROL for layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json's
`ties[]` declaration. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as
evidence about this block's well ties.
Byte-identical to the supply spec except for ONE token in the tie's
`tap_requires`: Poly2 30/0 instead of Nplus 32/0.
WHAT IT IS FOR. The committed supply run reports ZERO
`erc.missing_tie`, and a zero is only evidence if the check could have
produced a non-zero on this same stream. This control produces one.
WHY THE GATE MARKING AND NOT AN IMPLANT. Until issue #836 this control
narrowed on Pplus 31/0 -- then a genuine near-miss, because Pplus was
drawn only on the two substrate-tie guard rings, OUTSIDE every well, so
`COMP n Pplus` was a large non-empty region that never landed inside a
well. #836 draws source/drain implants (DR-0047): every PMOS S/D inside
every Nwell island now carries Pplus and reaches vdd through its
source terminals, so the Pplus-narrowed tap boolean finds a tap in
every well and the control collapses to `clean` -- measured, not
assumed: 0 findings, exit 4, on `adc_block.gds` sha256 `33f6f0c4…`.
With implants on all 323 devices' diffusion there is no longer any
drawn layer that marks COMP inside a well but only outside the taps,
so the discriminator moves from WHAT-is-marked to HOW: `COMP n Poly2`
is the *transistor* marking -- the channel-and-S/D stripe under every
gate, drawn in every one of the 25 wells -- and a tap is precisely
diffusion that is NOT part of a transistor. The region is large,
non-empty and inside every well (the same properties that made the
Pplus version discriminate before #836), but it is gate-marked, not
tap-marked, so every one of the 25 wells reports untapped.
EXPECTED OUTCOME: 25 `erc.missing_tie` findings and `erc_status:
"violations"`, from a NON-EMPTY tap region, with the rule checked
(no coverage skip).
That last clause is what distinguishes this control from the
`tie-narrowed` known-gap reproduction it replaced (issue #340,
DR-0032). That one declared the same narrowing this repo's supply spec
now uses, and got the same 25 findings -- but from an EMPTY tap region,
because the stream drew no implants at all. Its findings were
*unfounded*: it would have emitted them whatever the layout drew, so it
discriminated nothing. This one moves the marking, not the layout, and
goes red for a reason that depends on what the tap actually is. Flip
the supply spec's own narrowing to 30/0 by mistake and this control
and the artifact would swap verdicts, which is the property a control
is supposed to have.
`run_erc.py` re-runs it and asserts the outcome above.
